What ships today is the query, the cohort, the refusal stamp and the citation string — on this page the stamp fires on one system entirely and on ten of twelve landfall contracts for two others; exportable charts, an API and recurring institutional briefs are PROPOSED / PILOT.

sections.body: Four active systems, four declared points: 97L and 95E as pre-genesis reference cells, Karina and Lowell as observed genesis points. Three return a cohort deep enough to score. The fourth, Lowell, refuses every rate and shows its six storms anyway. Rates are genesis-conditioned and assume formation; scope and conditioning are stated in the footer and apply to every row below.

Highest commercial relevance. The cohort is anchored on the declared cell at 28.0°N 88.7°W, not on the disturbance, which now sits west and south of it. Alicia 1983 and Fern 1971 are in that cohort; so is Anita 1977, which came ashore in Tamaulipas rather than the US.

An intensity case, not an exposure case. Ten of twelve landfall contracts return a refusal stamp — nine OUT OF SCOPE, one BASE RATE ONLY — leaving the Mexico pair, any and ≥64 kt, as the only scored landfall rows. The eight printed cohort members, Kenneth 2017 and Guillermo 2009 among them, record no modelled landfall.
Watch candidate, and the deepest cohort on the page at 24 — the only one here that can be read down the full intensity ladder. No live archive record exists: 95E is pre-genesis and has no b-deck.

Nothing to price here. Every rate refused: six East Pacific storms against a minimum of 10, Hawaii included, where one of the six made landfall. Lowell is the control — the same query that returns 24 for 95E returns 6 here and the rates disappear. The refusal is about sample, not distance from land.

Cohort available and sufficient: 12 North Atlantic storms formed within 250 km of the declared cell, August–September, seasons from 1971, against a minimum sample of 10. The cell is a declared query point and the live centre now sits west and south of it. Sensitivity is declared, not hidden: hold the cell and tighten to 150 km and the cohort falls to 5, COHORT STATUS reads BELOW MIN SAMPLE — rates refused, and every row including CONUS — any and CONUS ≥64 kt reads RATE REFUSED; open the window to all months and the cohort rises to 17. The 12-storm answer is the 250 km August–September answer and nothing else.

At 250 km, intensity rows TD through Cat 5 and the CONUS, Mexico, Caribbean, Central America and unattributed landfall pairs are usable. Hawaii — any is stamped OUT OF SCOPE -- unscoreable here (0 in scope, 11 archive-wide) and Hawaii ≥64 kt BASE RATE ONLY -- unscoreable (0 in scope, 2 archive-wide, against the 10 required).

There is no Texas or Louisiana rate at any radius — landfall is scored at CONUS, not by state. The state is recorded on every landfall row: Alicia 1983 into Texas at 100 kt, Fern 1971 into Louisiana, Anita 1977 into Tamaulipas at 120 kt. The named history is state-level; the rate is not.

Cohort available and sufficient: 14 East Pacific storms formed within 250 km of the observed genesis point, August–September, since 1971. The intensity answer in full: TS 13 of 14 (92.9%, [69-99%]), Cat 1 7 of 14 (50.0%, [27-73%]), Cat 3 4 of 14 (28.6%, [12-55%]), Cat 4 1 of 14 (7.1%, [1-31%]), Cat 5 0 of 14 (0.0%, [0-22%]).

Mexico — any is 1 of 14 (7.1%, [1-31%]) and Mexico ≥64 kt is 0 of 14 (0.0%, [0-22%]). Those two are the only scored landfall rows. The other ten contracts return a stamp: nine OUT OF SCOPE -- unscoreable here, and Hawaii ≥64 kt BASE RATE ONLY -- unscoreable. The nine are refused on event counts, not on geography — each carries fewer than the 10 distinct in-scope events (EP basin, 1971 onwards) a score requires. CONUS — any has 2 in scope against 699 archive-wide, and the archive will not borrow the wider number.

Cohort available and sufficient: 24 East Pacific storms formed within 250 km of the declared reference cell, August–September, since 1971 — deep enough to read the ladder all the way down. TS 24 of 24 (100.0%, [86-100%]), Cat 1 15 of 24 (62.5%, [43-79%]), Cat 3 12 of 24 (50.0%, [31-69%]), Cat 4 6 of 24 (25.0%, [12-45%]), Cat 5 0 of 24 (0.0%, [0-14%]).

Landfall is a single storm. Mexico — any and Mexico ≥64 kt are both 1 of 24 (4.2%, [1-20%]), and the storm is Liza 1976 into Sonora at 90 kt. The stamps match Karina's — nine landfall contracts OUT OF SCOPE -- unscoreable here on in-scope event counts, Hawaii ≥64 kt BASE RATE ONLY -- unscoreable — and they are printed in the ledger.

Cohort below minimum sample — rates refused. Six East Pacific storms match the observed genesis point against a minimum of 10, so Storm Atlas refuses every rate on this row, intensity and landfall alike. The six stay visible as named history, Iniki 1992 among them. Widening is available and declared, never silent: the same pack ships a 97L variant opened to all months at N=17, published as its own query with its own citation string. Nothing was widened here, and the row is left empty.

The legend carries the mark types. What it cannot show: the two reference cells — 97L at 28.0°N 88.7°W and 95E at 12.0°N 107.5°W — are declared query points, not observed formations, and 97L's live centre and outlook area sit west and south of the cell its cohort is anchored on. Karina at 13.2°N 115.0°W and Lowell at 11.3°N 133.8°W are observed genesis points. All four rings are the same 250 km query radius, and the geometry says nothing about the result: three enclose scoring cohorts of 12, 14 and 24, while Lowell's encloses 6 and every rate inside it is refused. Live marks are 13:25 UTC 31 Aug 2026 and are not cohort geometry.

Lowell returns 6 against a minimum of 10, so every rate on that row refuses. Iniki 1992 is in that cohort with a Kauai landfall and it still does not become a percentage. The same rule empties 97L at 150 km, N=5. Hawaii ≥64 kt carries a BASE RATE ONLY stamp wherever it appears, on 2 events archive-wide against the 10 required. The thresholds are fixed and published; they are not adjusted to produce a row.

This is a sample-size floor and nothing more. It does not vouch for the track attribution, the landfall geocoding or the basin assignment. Those live in METHODOLOGY 1.1.0 / PACK 134661125525f27a, and they are what to audit.

sections.heading: What this dossier is
sections.body: Invest 97L is a live disturbance in the north-central Gulf. Storm Atlas does not forecast it and states no landfall for it. This dossier reports what the North Atlantic archive holds for the twelve storms that formed within 250 km of the declared pre-genesis reference cell 28.0°N 88.7°W, in August or September, in seasons from 1971 onwards: conditional on formation, silent on whether 97L forms.

sections.heading: Why 28.0°N 88.7°W and not the live centre
sections.body:
The query runs at a declared pre-genesis reference cell, 28.0°N 88.7°W — not the live centre near 27.4°N 90.7°W. 97L has not formed, so it has no observed genesis to query and no b-deck record in the archive's operational layer; the live centre also moves, and a published question does not.

The cell, the 250 km radius and the August–September window are analyst choices, declared before the query and not re-fitted after it. The cell was not derived from the live centre. The uncomfortable part, stated plainly: the same cell at 150 km returns N=5 and refuses every rate, so the published frame is a frame that clears the minimum sample where a tighter one does not. Read that as a constraint on what could be published, not as validation that this frame is the right one.

The question is: if a tropical cyclone were to form within 250 km of this cell, what happened historically to storms that formed there? It is silent on whether 97L forms, and on whether it would form inside the cell.

sections.heading: Reading the outcome panel
sections.body:
Every scoreable row is exact n/N with the 95% Wilson interval the engine returned. Two rows are not scoreable; an interval still prints beside them and is void. Read the interval, not the point estimate: at N=12 the bands are wide by construction and the archive will not narrow them.

The CONUS rows are two different questions. A crossing at any intensity is 10 of 12 (83.3%, 95% Wilson 55-95%); a crossing at hurricane force is 1 of 12 (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%).

Both Hawaii rows still print 0/12 and 0.0% [0-24%], and both carry a stamp that voids that figure: hawaii:any is OUT OF SCOPE for a North Atlantic cohort; hawaii:hurricane is BASE RATE ONLY, 2 events archive-wide against a 10-event minimum. The 0.0% is an artefact of the count, not a rate — do not read it as a low probability. That refusal costs nothing: no Gulf cohort could ever score Hawaii. The refusals that bite are elsewhere on this page — no state-level row exists at any sample size, and at 150 km this same cell refuses every rate in the panel.

sections.heading: Radius, month window and season floor
sections.body:
Three filters are declared in every citation this dossier rests on: radius, month window, and a 1971 season floor. Two of them are varied in this pack, and they decide both whether the instrument answers and what it answers.

At 250 km, August–September, seasons from 1971 onwards, the cohort is N=12 and the status is SUFFICIENT, so rates publish. Tighten the radius to 150 km and the cohort falls to N=5, below the minimum sample of 10, and every rate in the panel is REFUSED; the counts still print, the rates do not. Widen to all months at 250 km and the cohort is N=17, SUFFICIENT again — and the rows move: CONUS any goes to 13 of 17 (76.5%, 95% Wilson 53-90%), CONUS ≥64 kt to 2 of 17 (11.8%, 95% Wilson 3-34%).

Three frames, three counts on the row a hurricane-force trigger is written on: 1 of 12, 0 of 5 (refused), 2 of 17. The frame does not only decide whether the instrument answers; it moves the answer. That is why radius and month window sit in the published question rather than in a footnote, and why a buyer should ask what a frame they were not shown would have returned.

The 1971 season floor is the third filter and it is not varied here. This pack holds no floor-off variant, so this dossier cannot show what dropping the floor would do to N=12. It declares the filter and stops there.

sections.heading: Historical transit times
sections.body:
The minimum-sample rule governs published rates, not timing quantiles. The engine returns these unstamped at any n, so read them without assuming they passed the test the rate panel is held to.

Within this cohort the archive records a median 21 h from genesis to TS (n=10, p25 7.5, p75 33), a median 36 h to Cat 1 (n=3, p25 33, p75 84) and a median 72 h to Cat 3 (n=2, p25 69, p75 75). Only the TS figure clears the 10-case threshold. The Cat 1 figure is three storms — the same three the 3/12 Cat 1 rate is built on — and the Cat 3 figure is two; p25 and p75 across three numbers are a spread between three numbers, not a distribution.

Transit to a CONUS crossing is a median 65.5 h (n=22, p25 36.75, p75 176.25). Read n=22 as recorded landfall rows, not storms: 10 of the 12 cohort members crossed CONUS, and FERN 1971 contributes 12 of the 22 rows on its own — five Louisiana, seven Texas. Over half of that spread, including the 176.25 h upper quartile, is one 1971 track re-counted. The interquartile spread, not the median, is what this row actually constrains, and it is not a transit distribution over twelve independent cases.

These are historical intervals measured from each cohort member's own genesis. They are not a lead time for 97L, which has no genesis.

sections.heading: The analog plate
sections.body:
The plate prints up to eight members of the N=12 cohort under the archive's stated rule: majors (≥96 kt) first, then hurricanes (≥64 kt), then by peak wind descending, ties by season descending. Eight are printed here, so four members are not shown; none of them is above the 50 kt peak of the weakest printed member. That is a selection rule, not a relevance ranking, and it means the plate over-represents the intense end of the cohort.

Each printed member carries its genesis date, its distance from the declared cell, and its own recorded landfalls from the archive's landfalls table: ANITA 1977 peaked at 150 kt and came ashore in Tamaulipas, Mexico at 120 kt; ALICIA 1983 peaked at 100 kt and came ashore in Texas at 100 kt. Those are facts about named storms, not rates, and they are not counted into one.

Storm Atlas implements no similarity metric for a filter-defined cohort and weights every member 1.0, so no member is a closer or likelier match than another. The tracks drawn are history, not a cone.

sections.heading: COMMERCIAL READ — interpretation, not a rate
sections.body:
• Insured-region adjacency. The rows below are CONUS-wide, not Gulf-coast rows. The archive scores no sub-CONUS region, and this cohort's crossings include Florida landfalls alongside Texas and Louisiana ones, so against a Gulf-facing book they are a national-coastline prior, not a Gulf number. 10 of 12 crossed CONUS at any intensity (83.3%, 95% Wilson 55-95%); 1 of 12 crossed at ≥64 kt (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%). The second row is a subset of the first: in this cohort a crossing was ordinary and a hurricane-force crossing was one storm. An attachment set at hurricane force is being informed by a single archived event with a 1-35% band around it. Use it to bound or to challenge a rate set elsewhere; do not derive one from it.
  • Energy adjacency. The reference cell sits in north-central Gulf production and marine-logistics geography. The archive's transit to a CONUS crossing is a median 65.5 h (n=22, p25 36.75, p75 176.25) — and n=22 counts recorded landfall rows, not storms: 10 of the 12 members crossed, and FERN 1971 supplies 12 of the 22 rows. For shut-in and re-staging discussion, treat the upper quartile as one 1971 track's coastal history rather than as twelve independent cases. It is a historical statistic, not a schedule.
  • Parametric trigger questions this cohort can inform. How often did storms from this cell reach the class a trigger names — Cat 1 3 of 12 (25.0%, 95% Wilson 9-53%), Cat 3 2 of 12 (16.7%, 95% Wilson 5-45%)? How often did they cross CONUS at all versus at hurricane force? The verdict on the bands: an N=12 cohort returns intervals too wide to price a trigger. They will bound one, and they will show a counterparty exactly what the record does and does not contain.
  • BASIS RISK — same genesis cell does not mean same landfall. ANITA 1977 formed 126 km from this cell and struck Tamaulipas. ALICIA 1983 formed 194 km from it and struck Texas. One cell, two coasts.
  • BASIS RISK — same intensity class does not mean same local outcome. Peak intensity is not landfall intensity. FERN 1971 peaked at 80 kt; the archive records its Louisiana crossings at 25 kt and its Texas crossings between 43 and 60 kt. No landfall row for that storm reaches its peak.
  • BASIS RISK — a CONUS row is not a state row. The archive records state names in individual landfall rows; it publishes no state-level rate. CONUS and CONUS ≥64 kt are what exist. Any TX / LA / MS-AL-FL or Gulf-state rate would have to be manufactured, and none appears here.

sections.heading: What is not here
sections.body:
Refused by the instrument. No Hawaii rate: two rows on this panel returned unscoreable — hawaii:any OUT OF SCOPE for a North Atlantic cohort, hawaii:hurricane BASE RATE ONLY at 2 events archive-wide against a 10-event minimum — and no rate is published from either, though a 0.0% [0-24%] still prints beside them. No rates at all at 150 km: that cohort is N=5 and every row in the panel returned REFUSED.

Out of scope by contract, or not ours to give. No state-level landfall row. The archive records state names in individual landfall rows — the plate shows them — but publishes no state-level rate contract; CONUS and CONUS ≥64 kt are the rows that exist, and nothing in this dossier should be read as a sub-CONUS rate. No P(forms) from Storm Atlas: the engine is genesis-conditioned and takes formation as given, so the 70% / 70% (48h / 7d) on AL97 is the NHC's number, printed as theirs. The two numbers on this page do not chain. NHC's 70% is genesis anywhere in the Northern Gulf of America area it named; the archive's rows are conditional on genesis within 250 km of 28.0°N 88.7°W in August or September in seasons from 1971 onwards. Different conditioning sets, different producers, different scoring. Multiplying them assumes 97L forms inside the cell — that assumption is the reader's, not this dossier's, and no unconditional number is computed here. No forecast track, no cone, and no landfall call for 97L.

answers.now: Live status as of 31 Aug 2026, 08:25 CT / 13:25 UTC. Desk line at that instant: Invest 97L is a north-central Gulf disturbance near 27.4N 90.7W, about 100 mi south of Louisiana; the NHC graphical outlook the terminal ingested at 07:10Z carries AL97 “Northern Gulf of America” at 70% / 70% (48h / 7d) and describes a low “more than 100 miles south of the coast of southern Louisiana” — two sources, two instants, printed as they stand and not reconciled. Storm Atlas itself returns nothing on 97L: it is pre-genesis, has no b-deck, and the operational layer generated 2026-08-31T07:10Z holds no record for it. The cohort on this page is not that centre; it is the declared pre-genesis reference cell at 28.0N 88.7W.
answers.adds: The alternative is not a public map — it is your own IBTrACS or HURDAT2 query, which a cat modelling team can write. What Storm Atlas supplies is the discipline around that query: a question fixed before the answer, exact n/N with the 95% Wilson interval, the named members behind every rate, a pinned methodology and pack stamp, and a URL a counterparty reopens to the same members and the same refusals. Refusal runs on two counts — where the cohort is too thin to score, and where the contract itself carries too few events in this basin and era — so a sufficient cohort can still return refused rows, as this one does.
answers.commercial: It gives a basis-risk file one component that can be tested: a cohort the counterparty reopens from a URL and reproduces line for line, misses included. It is not an event set, not a hazard footprint, not a payout model, and it does not price. It carries no forecast, no skill claim and no price call.

sections.body: Storm Atlas is a research-only historical engine. It answers one fixed question — from this declared genesis condition, in this season window, what did the record go on to do — and returns exact n/N with the 95% Wilson interval, or refuses to return a rate. The refusals, the named members and the replay URL are printed alongside every rate, so the specification can be attacked rather than accepted.

sections.heading: Why a replayable cohort is trigger documentation
sections.body:
• The cohort is a declared judgement, not a hidden one. Five choices set it and each one moves the answer: basin, centre, radius, season floor, month window. Here — North Atlantic, 28.0°N 88.7°W, 250 km, August–September, seasons from 1971 onwards — a pre-genesis reference cell, declared in advance of the query and distinct from the live centre. Attack the choices: all five are on the page and each variant has its own URL.
  • Every published rate is exact n/N and the 95% Wilson interval the engine returned. Nothing is smoothed, weighted, blended or fitted. Where the engine refused, no rate is printed — the refusal is printed in its place.
  • Every block carries a cite line and a replay URL encoding the same parameters. A counterparty pastes the URL, reopens the identical cohort, and gets the identical members, rates and refusals. The refusal is checkable on the same terms: the 150 km variant reopens from its own URL (…&w=28,-88.7,150&s0=1971&mo=8.9&b=NA&m=1.1.0), where every row returns RATE REFUSED. The refusal is reproducible evidence, not an assurance.
  • Provenance, not just a hash. Built from IBTrACS and HURDAT2 best-track files for the North Atlantic and East Pacific; pinned as methodology 1.1.0, pack 134661125525f27a, built 2026-08-18T05:18:57Z over 3,959 storms, 224,153 track points and 3,379 landfall rows. Read the composition, not the totals: of the 224,153 track points, 114,316 are observed, 109,171 interpolated and 666 provisional; landfall category is withheld on 466 of the 3,379 landfall rows; 1,305 landfalls are detected from the HURDAT2 L-record, 1,061 from a bracketing fix and 1,013 from segment crossing. The replay URL pins the question and the methodology version, not the build — the pack stamp printed beside every rate identifies the build the number came from, so a rebuilt archive after a reanalysis carries a different stamp and the change is visible rather than silent.
  • Timing is reported per landfall row, not per storm. Time to CONUS landfall is n=22 rows against a cohort of 12 storms — median 65.5 h, p25 36.75, p75 176.25 — and Fern 1971 alone carries twelve CONUS landfall rows in the archive. Treat the spread as the range the record covers, not as a storm-level median, and reweight before an observation window is argued from it.

sections.heading: Near-misses: where the basis risk is
sections.body:
A near-miss is a cohort member that satisfies the genesis rule and then fails the condition a trigger would be written on.

  • In the cohort — Anita 1977. Formed 126 km from the cell; came ashore in Tamaulipas, Mexico at 120 kt. Inside the cohort, outside the CONUS row.
  • In the cohort — Fern 1971. Formed 131 km out and peaked at 80 kt, but its landfall rows are Louisiana at 25 kt and Texas topping out at 60 kt.
  • In the cohort — Alicia 1983. Formed 194 km out and came ashore in Texas at 100 kt — the single member standing behind CONUS — ≥64 kt at 1 of 12 (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%). That is a CONUS row, not a Texas one: the archive does not score state-level landfall, and the state is a fact about Alicia rather than a rate. It is not a member at 150 km. Tighten the radius that way and the cohort falls to 5 against a minimum sample of 10 and every row REFUSES, including CONUS — ≥64 kt, which returns a refusal at 0 of 5, not a zero. The membership change is visible; no rate at 150 km is.
  • Excluded by the window — Barry 2019. Formed 110 km from the cell with a 65 kt Louisiana landfall, but its 11 July genesis falls outside August–September: it is not in this cohort at all. It appears in the separately published season-wide variant of the same cell — 250 km, all months, seasons from 1971, N=17 — which is a different cohort with its own rates and its own replay URL. It is also the closest thing in the record to the event a trigger here would be written for, and this cohort does not contain it. Read the misses first: that is where a trigger fails to pay while the underlying event still occurs.

sections.heading: Basis risk — read before writing the trigger
sections.body:
• Same genesis cell is not the same landfall. Anita 1977 and Alicia 1983 both formed inside this cell in this window. Anita's landfall was Tamaulipas, Mexico at 120 kt; Alicia's was Texas at 100 kt. The cell constrains where a storm started, nothing else.
  • Same class is not the same local outcome. CONUS — any is 10 of 12 (83.3%, 95% Wilson 55-95%). CONUS — ≥64 kt is 1 of 12 (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%), and that single member is Alicia 1983. A coastal crossing is common in this cohort; a crossing at hurricane force is not, and a trigger keyed to intensity at the coast sits on the second number and on one storm.
  • The CONUS row is not a state row. The archive scores landfall by region. In this cohort conus, mexico, caribbean, central_america and unattributed are scored; both hawaii rows are refused (hawaii — any: OUT OF SCOPE -- unscoreable here; hawaii — ≥64 kt: BASE RATE ONLY -- unscoreable). It does not score state-level landfall at all. There is no Texas rate, no Louisiana rate, no sub-CONUS rate here, and this document will not manufacture one. A named member's own landfall is a fact from the landfalls table; it is not a frequency and must not be counted into one.
  • The Wilson width at N=12 is the precision, not a rounding artefact. CONUS — any carries 55-95%; CONUS — ≥64 kt carries 1-35%. Which bound binds depends on which side of the risk the reader sits: a protection buyer is exposed at 95% and 35%, a seller at 55% and 1%, and twelve storms will not close the gap between them. A midpoint treated as tight asserts a precision the record does not contain.
  • The rate moves with the specification — in both directions. Tighten the radius to 150 km and the cohort falls to 5 against a minimum sample of 10; every row is refused rather than published thin. Widen the month window instead, from August–September to all months, and the cohort rises to 17: CONUS — any falls to 13 of 17 (76.5%, 95% Wilson 53-90%) and CONUS — ≥64 kt rises to 2 of 17 (11.8%, 95% Wilson 3-34%). Both variants have their own replay URL. Fix the specification before the answer is visible, and show the counterparty the variants that were not used.
  • Refused, unscoreable and withheld are not zeros. The 150 km cohort is refused on sample. Separately, two rows are unscoreable on their own evidence: hawaii — any is OUT OF SCOPE -- unscoreable here, 0 in scope in this basin and era against 11 archive-wide, 10 required; hawaii — ≥64 kt is BASE RATE ONLY -- unscoreable, 0 in scope against 2 archive-wide. Both print 0 of 12 [0-24%] under those flags; neither is a scored zero and neither may enter a structure as a probability. Landfall category is withheld on 466 of the archive's 3,379 landfall rows. All three states mean the same thing — the record does not support a number at that specification. None of them is evidence about the hazard.
  • These rates are genesis-conditioned and assume formation. They are not P(forms), not a live feed and not a forecast for any running system. The NHC 70% / 70% development odds on AL97 are a separate quantity from a separate source, printed with its own instant, and it does not multiply into these rows.

sections.heading: Where this sits in the workflow
sections.body:
Upstream of pricing: cohort research, trigger design, and counterparty explanation, where a replay URL lets the other side reproduce the number instead of taking it on trust. What the record supports here, stated plainly:

  • A trigger keyed to any CONUS crossing sits on 10 of 12 — 83.3%, 55-95%.
  • One keyed to hurricane force at the coast sits on 1 of 12 — 8.3%, 1-35% — resting on a single member, and twelve storms will not resolve it tighter.
  • An observation window closing before 36.75 h from genesis catches at most the earliest quarter of this cohort's 22 CONUS landfall rows; one closing before 176.25 h still misses the latest quarter.
  • A region row finer than CONUS does not exist in this archive, so a state- or parish-keyed trigger cannot be documented from this page at all.

Those are the answers the record supports. The page will not manufacture a fifth. This is not live pricing of a running event: Storm Atlas states what the record did from a declared cell and makes no claim about where 97L goes. The cite line and replay URL exist today; exportable charts, an API and recurring institutional briefs are proposed / pilot, not shipping.

What it supplies is frequency bands with their cohorts and refusals open to inspection. It prices nothing, forecasts nothing and recommends nothing.

sections.heading: Gulf genesis, scored against the record
sections.body:
As of 31 Aug 2026, 08:25 CT / 13:25 UTC, the desk has Invest 97L as a north-central Gulf disturbance at 27.4°N 90.7°W; the NHC outlook ingested at 07:10Z carries AL97 at 70% / 70% (48h / 7d). Storm Atlas does not forecast that system and makes no claim about where it goes. It scores what North Atlantic storms did from a declared pre-genesis reference cell at 28.0°N 88.7°W, within 250 km, in August or September, in seasons from 1971 onwards — assuming formation.

That cell is not 97L's position. It sits north and east of the desk fix, it is a fixed query point, and every row on this page is scored from it rather than from the live system. The 250 km aperture is what makes the cohort scoreable at all: the same cell at 150 km returns N=5 against min sample 10, and every rate there is refused. This page prints the cohort, the intervals, and the status the archive returned on each row — including the rows it refuses to score.

sections.heading: Geography is not a probability
sections.body:
Landfall resolves to region, not state. The archive scores CONUS, Mexico, Caribbean, Central America, Hawaii and unattributed, each in an "any" and a ">=64 kt" form — and of those it refuses both Hawaii rows on this cohort. There is no Texas row, no Louisiana row and no Gulf-state row to quote: the archive does not score states at all, so CONUS and CONUS >=64 kt are the rows that bear on a Gulf question.

The paths on the plate are drawn tracks of named cohort members — the 8 representatives the query prints, out of the cohort of 12 the rates are scored on — exactly as the archive holds them. Where a track runs is geography read off the archive. It is not a scored state probability, and nothing on this page counts or tallies tracks by state.

Genesis-conditioned, assuming formation: CONUS — any 10 of 12 (83.3%, 95% Wilson 55-95%) and CONUS — >=64 kt 1 of 12 (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%). A member's own landfall stays a fact about that storm — ALICIA 1983 came ashore in Texas at 100 kt — and is never aggregated into a rate.

sections.heading: Commercial reading — what the rows cover
sections.body:
• Two hurricane landfalls, opposite sides of the basin. The cohort's scored hurricane rows are CONUS — >=64 kt at 1 of 12 (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%) and MEXICO — >=64 kt at 1 of 12 (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%). ANITA 1977 is the Mexican one, ashore in Tamaulipas at 120 kt; ALICIA 1983 is the CONUS one, ashore in Texas at 100 kt. Both rows are regions. Neither is a terminal, a platform or a refinery.
  • Severity resolution. The intensity ladder is all the archive publishes: reached TS 10 of 12 (83.3%, 95% Wilson 55-95%), Cat 1 3 of 12 (25.0%, 9-53%), Cat 3 2 of 12 (16.7%, 5-45%), Cat 5 1 of 12 (8.3%, 1-35%). Cat 3 is the severity step most energy exposure is written around; on this cohort that row is two members wide.
  • Timing. Both timing rows are clocked from genesis and count events, not storms. TIME TO ts: n=10, median 21 h (p25 7.5, p75 33). TIME TO landfall_conus: n=22, median 65.5 h (p25 36.75, p75 176.25) — 22 landfall crossings, not 22 storms; members that came ashore more than once contribute more than once, and only 10 of the 12 reached CONUS at all. 97L has no genesis clock running, so neither row is a lead time for it.
  • Geography, not assets. The reference cell sits in the north-central Gulf. The archive holds track points and landfall rows — not lease blocks, terminals, refineries or grid nodes — so proximity to the drawn geography is the whole of what can be said. CONUS is the finest landfall resolution the archive scores; state resolution does not exist as a row, so there is no state row to refuse.
  • Not scored. Production, throughput, liquefaction windows, outage counts, restoration. No proxy for any of them is published here, and none should be constructed from the rows above.

sections.heading: Read the band, not the point
sections.body:
Every scored row is a band. CONUS — >=64 kt on this cohort is 1 of 12 (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%), and the interval, not the 8.3%, is the research input. Twelve members makes it wide by construction: one member moves the answer by a twelfth.

Tightening the aperture does not buy precision — it removes the answer. The same cell at 150 km returns N=5 against min sample 10, and the archive refuses every rate and every interval on that cohort: CONUS — any stands at 4 of 5 and CONUS — >=64 kt at 0 of 5, with RATE REFUSED printed in place of both the rate and the interval. Replay it: ?v=1&w=28,-88.7,150&s0=1971&mo=8.9&b=NA&m=1.1.0.

Widening moves the answer little. The same cell across all months returns N=17, CONUS — any 13 of 17 (76.5%, 95% Wilson 53-90%), CONUS — >=64 kt 2 of 17 (11.8%, 95% Wilson 3-34%). Three apertures, one refused and two overlapping. That is the whole robustness the record supports on this cell. A 1-35% band bounds the question and shows the cohort behind it; it does not support a point estimate, a load factor or a spread, and no aperture here will make it tighter. If a note needs a number tighter than that band, this cohort is not the source.

sections.heading: What this is not
sections.body:
No prices, no trades, no view on gas, power, refined products or freight. No state rates — the archive does not score states, and no named member's landfall is converted into one. Rows are genesis-conditioned and assume formation: not P(forms), not a cone, not a track for 97L. The NHC advisory is the forecast; this is the record standing behind it, and no forecast skill is claimed.

Two rows this archive holds are not scored here at all. On this cohort hawaii:any returns OUT OF SCOPE -- unscoreable here — 0 in scope in the North Atlantic since 1971, 11 archive-wide against the 10 required — and hawaii:hurricane returns BASE RATE ONLY -- unscoreable — 0 in scope, 2 archive-wide against the 10 required. Those are the archive's refusals, not ours.

sections.body:
The archive's operational layer (atlas-live-v1, generated 2026-08-31T07:10Z) holds the last fix it has: 06:00Z, 31 Aug 2026, 17.2°N 124.0°W, 120 kt, 945 mb, peak 120 kt, active. The cohort record, all seven intensity rows: TD 14 of 14 (100.0%, 95% Wilson 78-100%); TS 13 of 14 (92.9%, 95% Wilson 69-99%); Cat 1 7 of 14 (50.0%, 95% Wilson 27-73%); Cat 2 6 of 14 (42.9%, 95% Wilson 21-67%); Cat 3 4 of 14 (28.6%, 95% Wilson 12-55%); Cat 4 1 of 14 (7.1%, 95% Wilson 1-31%); Cat 5 0 of 14 (0.0%, 95% Wilson 0-22%).

Pathway timings, as the engine returned them: time to TS n=13, median 12 h (p25 6, p75 36); time to Cat 1 n=7, median 42 h (p25 39, p75 54); time to Cat 3 n=4, median 84 h (p25 70.5, p75 117); time to Mexico landfall n=1, median 99 h. Timings print with their n and carry no minimum-sample gate — n=4 and n=1 sit below the 10 distinct events the engine requires before it will publish a rate. Read them as the cohort's observed spread, not as scored quantities, and not as a schedule for Karina.

sections.heading: Where Karina sits against her genesis cohort
sections.body:
Two rows bear on Karina's current band. Cat 4 was reached by 1 of 14 (7.1%, 95% Wilson 1-31%); Cat 5 by 0 of 14 (0.0%, 95% Wilson 0-22%). That single Cat 4 is KENNETH 2017 at 115 kt, also the highest peak among the eight cohort members the engine printed: KENNETH 2017 115 kt, GUILLERMO 2009 110 kt, JOVA 2005 110 kt, JULIO 2014 105 kt, ORLENE 2016 95 kt, HECTOR 2006 95 kt, FERNANDA 2005 75 kt, FERNANDA 1999 55 kt — 8 printed, shortfall 0, none with a modelled landfall. They are printed under the query's filter rule, in descending peak intensity; Storm Atlas implements no similarity metric, ranks no member as a closest analog and names none. Both Karina instants, 120 kt and 125 kt, stand above every printed member, and no cohort member reached Cat 5.

The interval on that Cat 4 row runs 1-31% on a denominator of fourteen — too wide to carry a rarity claim. Storm Atlas computes no percentile and no return period: fourteen storms define neither a basin nor a season denominator. That is a scope limit of a genesis cohort, not a stamped refusal. The stamped refusals are the ten land contracts below.

sections.heading: Land rows, printed as the engine returned them
sections.body:
Twelve land contracts returned. Two carry rates: Mexico — any 1 of 14 (7.1%, 95% Wilson 1-31%); Mexico — ≥64 kt 0 of 14 (0.0%, 95% Wilson 0-22%). Nine returned OUT OF SCOPE -- unscoreable here: CONUS — any, CONUS — ≥64 kt, Caribbean — any, Caribbean — ≥64 kt, Central America — any, Central America — ≥64 kt, Hawaii — any, Unattributed — any, Unattributed — ≥64 kt. One returned BASE RATE ONLY -- unscoreable: Hawaii — ≥64 kt. That is all twelve rows the contract defines. The archive does not score state-level or sub-CONUS landfall at all; CONUS and CONUS — ≥64 kt are what exist, and here both are stamped.

  • CONUS — any, OUT OF SCOPE -- unscoreable here: 2 storms in scope (EP basin since 1971) carry the outcome against the 10 distinct events any skill score requires; the archive holds 699 in total, outside the population this query draws from. In the engine's words, a skill number over a population that does not carry the events would be borrowed from one that does.
  • Hawaii — ≥64 kt, BASE RATE ONLY -- unscoreable: 1 event in scope (EP basin since 1971), 2 archive-wide, 10 required. The row value, 0 of 14 (0.0%, 95% Wilson 0-22%), is quotable as a base rate only. A calibrated or skill-scored probability cannot be, and this archive will not produce one.

For a genesis cell in the East Pacific the archive's entire scoreable land exposure is Mexico, and one of those two rows is a zero. A zero with an interval is a result and a stamped row is a result; an omitted row is neither, so none are dropped and no broader cohort is substituted to fill one.

sections.heading: Commercial reading — labelled interpretation
sections.body: Karina has already passed both climb milestones this cohort times; the timings printed above are history, not a schedule for her. What the cohort does support is where she stands: above every printed member of her own genesis cell, on a fourteen-storm denominator whose only scoreable land exposure is Mexico, whose Mexico — ≥64 kt row is a zero, and whose other ten land contracts the archive declines to score with a stated reason each. That is the frame this page gives a researcher or a client-facing analyst — a stated denominator, an interval on every rate, and the refusals visible next to them. Nothing here is threat monitoring, a forecast, a track or a landfall claim about Karina. The archive scores genesis-conditioned landfall rows for the cohort, printed above; it scores no row about where a live storm goes, and this brief does not manufacture one. No price call, no trade view, no skill claim.

answers.adds: The outlook gives a disturbance a chance of forming; the cone gives a track if it does. Neither says that twelve North Atlantic storms formed within 250 km of the declared 97L reference cell in August or September since 1971, that ten of them reached TS, that one reached CONUS at ≥64 kt, or which twelve they were. Storm Atlas answers that question and no other — the denominator named, the 95% Wilson interval attached, and a visible refusal wherever the record cannot carry a rate: a cohort below the min sample, a contract out of scope for the basin, or an outcome too rare archive-wide to score at all.
answers.commercial: Worked, on this page: the 97L cohort returns CONUS ≥64 kt at 1/12 — 8.3%, 95% Wilson 1–35% — genesis-conditioned, on a denominator a counterparty can open and read storm by storm. The interval, not the point, is what a candidate trigger has to survive; landfall region and intensity are counted jointly and are never multiplied against each other; the footer states the one rule for combining a genesis-conditioned rate with a formation probability, and Storm Atlas supplies neither that probability nor the product. That is the input to trigger-threshold research, structuring and client explanation — a denominator you can name, a cohort you can list, an interval you cannot argue away, and a figure that does not move between readings under the same methodology version and pack hash. Storm Atlas makes no price call, no trade recommendation and no skill claim.

sections.body: Storm Atlas is a research-only historical genesis/outcome engine for the North Atlantic and East Pacific. Give it an observed genesis point or a declared pre-genesis reference cell; it returns what the record did next as exact n/N with a 95% Wilson interval, names every storm in the denominator, and refuses the rate where the record cannot carry one.

• Condition on a point. An observed genesis position, or a declared pre-genesis reference cell, with a stated radius and month window. The season floor is a declared boundary, not a preference: an observing-bias gap before 1971 is why the floor sits at 1971, and a cohort reaching behind it is warned rather than pooled silently. Rates are genesis-conditioned and assume formation — not P(forms), not a live feed, not a forecast cone.
  • Retrieve the analog tracks. Every storm in the cohort, with representative members printed under a stated rule — name, season, genesis date, distance from the cell, lifetime peak, and its own landfalls as recorded. Storm Atlas implements no similarity metric, so nothing is ranked as a closest or best analog.
  • Compare contract-row frequencies. Reached TD, TS and Cat 1 through Cat 5, each as exact n/N with its 95% Wilson interval. Time-to-threshold medians with p25 and p75 sit alongside and carry their own n: the min-sample gate governs rates, not medians, so a median can be printed on an n of one or two. Read the n before the median.
  • Inspect the landfall contract rows. conus, mexico, caribbean, central_america, hawaii and unattributed, each with an "any" and a ≥64 kt pair — but which of the twelve score is a property of the cohort, not of the archive: the Karina panel scores the mexico pair and refuses the other ten. State-level and sub-CONUS landfall is not scored at all. Sub-region is carried in the archive and can be read off a named storm's own landfall record; it is not a contract row, and no state-level rate exists.
  • Read the refusals as first-class output. Three gates, all printed. A cohort below min sample publishes counts and no rates at all — no rate column, no interval. A contract out of scope for the basin, or an outcome too rare archive-wide to score, prints its status beside a figure the status voids: where the status column is set, the 0.0% and the interval on that row are not results and must not be read as a zero. Hawaii ≥64 kt is base rate only — 2 archive-wide against the 10 required — and is never a scored probability.
  • Carry it into the work. Set a candidate intensity or landfall threshold and count the cohort members that cross it; they are named, so the count is checkable. Stress the cell before quoting anything — move it, and watch N and the refusal state move with it. Hand a reviewer the URL instead of a number. Environment — shear, mid-level RH, SST, OHC — is displayed against the cohort you already chose; it never changes who is in it.

An interpolated fix is never allowed to establish a threshold crossing, so time-to-hurricane is never dated off a wind nobody measured. A segment crossing publishes no Saffir-Simpson class where the two bracketing fixes disagree on it — the interpolated wind stays on the row, labelled by detection method; the class derived from it does not. A cohort's defining variable is not reported back as a scored outcome, with one exception left in the open: every cohort returns reached TD at 100%, because a cohort is storms that formed. That row is definitional and carries no information; the panels here start at reached TS. Below min sample a rate is refused rather than estimated — the same 97L cell read at 150 km instead of 250 km returns 5 storms against a min sample of 10, and every rate on that panel reads RATE REFUSED. A cohort reaching behind 1971 carries the observing-bias warning instead of pooling the record silently. An absent outcome is not a zero: an unrecorded intensity leaves the denominator and is counted on its own, so an n/N row can carry a smaller N than its cohort — no sample on this sheet exercises it, and every row runs on 12, on 14 and on 6. Every figure, refusals included, carries METHODOLOGY 1.1.0, PACK 134661125525f27a and a URL that reproduces it.

Delivery today is a browser and replayable cohort URLs. A URL carries the cell, radius, season floor, month window, basin and methodology version, so a colleague, a client or a reviewer opens the same cohort and reads the same counts, the same rates and intervals where the engine scored them, and the same refusals where it did not. It reproduces under the same pack stamp: the pack is a hash of every table it was built from, so a rebuilt archive changes the stamp, and a figure whose stamp does not match is not the same figure.
PROPOSED / PILOT — not available today. Exportable charts. An API. Recurring institutional briefs. None of the three exists yet.

Three cohorts follow, printed as the engine returned them. The cell is an input, not an observation: 97L is read at a desk-declared pre-genesis reference cell, 28.0°N 88.7°W — not the disturbance's current position, not the outlook area. Storm Atlas does not choose the cell and does not defend it; the URL records what was chosen, so a reviewer can move it and watch the answer move. Cohort N 12 at 250 km; the same cell read at 150 km returns 5, below the min sample of 10, every rate refused — which is why the radius is printed with the number. Karina is read at its observed genesis, 13.2°N 115.0°W, a datum rather than a choice, cohort N 14. It is the harder sample and it is here for that reason: the cohort returns reached Cat 4 at 1/14 [1–31%] and reached Cat 5 at 0/14 [0–22%], and Karina is already Cat 4. That is what a genesis-conditioned rate is — the record's frequency at the moment of formation. The cohort does not know Karina intensified and will not be revised because it did. Sample 3 is TS Lowell, read at its observed genesis 11.3°N 133.8°W: cohort N 6, below min sample, counts published and every rate refused — including the Hawaii rows, 1 of 6, where the one is Iniki 1992. A six-storm Hawaii rate is the number a desk would most want and the one the engine will not print. Scored rows carry exact n/N and the 95% Wilson interval; a status voids the figure beside it; a cohort below min sample returns no rate and no interval at all. Every figure replays from the URL beneath its table.

_edits.change: Added an explicit non-attribution clause after the Alicia 1983 bullet.
_edits.why: The bullet named a state and a CONUS rate in one block with nothing between them. Every claim in it is correct and traced, but a reader skimming the bullet could carry 8.3% away as a Texas number, which is the exact failure the state-level rule exists to prevent. scripts/check-collateral.mjs fails on that arrangement; the clause is what clears it, and it adds a statement rather than removing one.
